lessons.title: Friends of 5

stepByStep: Pick a number.
Think: what does it need to make 5?
Find that number right next to it and merge them.
play.kidTip: Count the dots on two tiles side by side. If there are 5 altogether, merge them.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Bonds to 5 are the first part-whole facts; dots let a child count before they recall.

play.kidTip: Look at the dots and the number together. 3 and 2 make 5.

lessons.title: Numbers to 5

play.kidTip: Think of the pairs: 1 and 4, 2 and 3.

play.kidTip: Dots come in rows of five. Two full rows make 10.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Making 10 is the key to adding and taking away across ten.

play.kidTip: 7 needs 3. 6 needs 4. Find the partner next to it.

lessons.title: Same and Same

play.targetObjective: Merge two numbers that are the same.
stepByStep: Find two tiles with the same number.
Merge them: the new number is double.
Keep going until you reach the goal.
play.kidTip: Find two tiles that look the same. 3 and 3 make 6.
play.audioPrompt: Merge two numbers that are the same.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Doubles are the easiest facts to remember and the base for near doubles.

lessons.title: Doubles to 20

play.targetObjective: Merge two numbers that are the same.
stepByStep: Find two tiles with the same number.
Merge them: the new number is double.
Keep going until you reach the goal.
play.kidTip: Double 6 is 12. Double 7 is 14.
play.audioPrompt: Merge two numbers that are the same.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Doubles are the easiest facts to remember and the base for near doubles.

lessons.title: Double Up to 16

play.targetObjective: Merge the same numbers to double them. Make 16.
stepByStep: Find two tiles with the same number.
Merge them: the new number is double.
Keep going until you reach the goal.
play.kidTip: Make two the same, then merge them. 2 and 2 make 4, 4 and 4 make 8.
play.audioPrompt: Merge the same numbers to double them. Make 16.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Doubles are the easiest facts to remember and the base for near doubles.

lessons.title: Double Up to 64

play.kidTip: Plan ahead: build two of the same before you merge.
play.audioPrompt: Merge the same numbers to double them. Make 64.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Doubles are the easiest facts to remember and the base for near doubles.

lessons.title: Reach 10

stepByStep: Merge small numbers to make bigger ones.
Watch the total: it must not go over 10.
Finish with the tile that makes exactly 10.
play.kidTip: Before you merge, add the two numbers in your head. Is it still 10 or less?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Planning sums to an exact target practises adding several numbers and estimating.

lessons.title: Ten Ones Make a Ten

play.targetObjective: Merge ones to make a ten.
stepByStep: Merge ones with ones until you have exactly 10.
A ten is a new tile.
Keep making tens.
play.kidTip: Count the dots. Stop when you have exactly 10.
play.audioPrompt: Merge ones to make a ten.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Ten ones become one ten: the idea behind place value.

lessons.title: Tens Make a Hundred

play.targetObjective: Merge ones into tens, and tens into a hundred.
stepByStep: Merge ones with ones until you have exactly 10.
A ten is a new tile.
Merge tens with tens until you have exactly 100.
play.kidTip: Ones go with ones and tens go with tens. Ten tens make one hundred.
play.audioPrompt: Merge ones into tens, and tens into a hundred.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Ten ones become one ten: the idea behind place value.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Building a product from factors connects multiplication facts and division.

lessons.title: Halves and Quarters

play.targetObjective: Merge parts to make one whole.
stepByStep: Merge two pieces to add them.
Watch the pie fill up.
Stop at one whole: a full pie.
play.kidTip: Two quarters make a half. A half and a half make one whole.
play.audioPrompt: Merge parts to make one whole.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Adding like fractions to one whole builds fraction sense with pictures first.

lessons.title: Friends of 20

stepByStep: Pick a number.
Use the 10 fact you know: 7 needs 3 to make 10.
So 7 needs 13 to make 20. Find it next to your number and merge.
play.kidTip: Make 10 first in your head, then add another 10.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Bonds to 20 are bonds to 10 with a ten added; the board rewards using the fact a child already holds.

lessons.title: Make 20 on a Big Board

stepByStep: Look for a big number first, like 15 or 18.
Ask: what does it need to make 20?
Find that partner right next to it and merge.
play.kidTip: Big numbers need small partners: 18 needs 2.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A bigger board means more pairs to scan, which moves a child from counting on towards recall.

lessons.title: Multiply to 20

stepByStep: Merging multiplies the two numbers.
Finish with two numbers that multiply to 20.
play.kidTip: Think of the 2, 5 and 10 times tables. Which ones land on 20?

lessons.pedagogyTip: The 2, 5 and 10 tables come first; 20 can be built from all three.

lessons.title: Multiply to 30

stepByStep: Merging multiplies the two numbers.
Only keep numbers that are part of 30's times facts.
play.kidTip: 2 × 3 makes 6, and 6 × 5 makes 30. Build one part first.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Three small factors (2, 3, 5) can be merged in any order and still reach 30.

lessons.title: Multiply to 60

stepByStep: 60 has many factor pairs: 6 × 10, 5 × 12, 4 × 15, 3 × 20.
Merge small numbers into a factor of 60.
Finish with two numbers that multiply to 60.
play.kidTip: If a merge makes a number that does not go into 60, it will not be allowed.

lessons.pedagogyTip: 60 has more factors than any number before it, so a child has to plan which pair to build.

lessons.title: Thirds and Sixths
lessons.concept: Sixths, Thirds and Halves Make One Whole

play.targetObjective: Merge parts to make one whole.
stepByStep: The pies show sixths, thirds and halves.
Change each one into sixths: a third is 2 sixths, a half is 3 sixths.
Merge until you have 6 sixths. That is one whole.
play.kidTip: 1/2 is 3 sixths and 1/3 is 2 sixths. Add the sixths until you have 6.
play.audioPrompt: Merge parts to make one whole.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A third and a half are both sixths; the pie shows why 1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2.

lessons.title: Tenths to One
lessons.concept: Tenths, Fifths and Halves Make One Whole

play.targetObjective: Merge parts to make one whole.
stepByStep: The pies show tenths, fifths and halves.
Change each one into tenths: a fifth is 2 tenths, a half is 5 tenths.
Merge until you have 10 tenths. That is one whole.
play.kidTip: 1/2 is 5 tenths and 1/5 is 2 tenths. Add the tenths until you have 10.
play.audioPrompt: Merge parts to make one whole.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Tenths are the bridge to decimals: one whole is ten tenths, as 1.0 is ten lots of 0.1.
